d: Forget beach holidays and mountain getaways. A new kind of tourism is drawing crowds and it takes people to places associated with death, disaster and tragedy. From spending the night in a house where a notorious murder took place to experiencing a simulated typhoon, tourists are actively seeking out fear, shock and the macabre. This is called dark tourism - and it is becoming a multi-billion-dollar industry. But where does curiosity end and exploitation begin? Palki Sharma tells you.
